reports.title: LIVE NATION ENTERTAINMENT REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS

lines: We now expect to welcome nearly 180 million fans in 2026.

desk.headline: Revenue up 19% to a record $10.1bn, beat; diluted EPS $1.69 vs $1.50 expected; fan count now seen near 180m for 2026
results: Record quarter: revenue rose 19% to $10.1bn, operating income 13% to $892m and AOI 14% to $1.18bn, with all three segments growing AOI by double digits.
Concerts drew 61m fans (+19%); international attendance rose 29% and made up 60% of the growth, while North America rose 13%.
Ticketmaster sold a record 98m fee-bearing tickets (+10%); resale value was flat as sports offset weaker concert resale.
Sponsorship revenue grew 14% to $506m; international sponsorship now earns more than North America.
Year-to-date operating cash flow was $2.1bn (+45%) and adjusted free cash flow $1.6bn (+25%); capex is heading for nearly $1.1bn this year, mostly on venues.

guidance.summary: No revenue or profit range is given. The company expects nearly 180m fans in 2026, double-digit AOI growth in Concerts and Sponsorship, and high single-digit AOI growth at Ticketmaster.

points: The CFO said ticket on-sales for big 2027 tours already give the business momentum going into next year.
Management said consumer demand remains strong across its venues worldwide.
The Ticketmaster outlook was lifted to high single-digit AOI growth for 2026, helped by over 20m net new tickets this year.
Venue Nation expects about 75m fans this year; owned venues earn more per fan, but opening costs will rise in coming years.
Questions on venue spending and capital use were held over to an investor day; the antitrust case was not discussed in detail on the call.
call.source: Call transcript (Benzinga, via Webull) and TicketNews, 6 Nov 2026

watch: Details at the upcoming investor day on venue investment and longer-term growth targets.
Progress of the antitrust case and any settlement affecting Ticketmaster.
Whether 2027 ticket sales keep running ahead of last year, especially in North America.
